recent_posts.title: janhq/jan: Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer
recent_posts.summary: Jan is an open-source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer. It supports universal architectures, has different version types for different operating systems, and offers both stable and experimental builds. Jan requires specific system requirements and can be run in different modes, such as CPU or GPU. Contributions are welcome and users can report bugs and make feature requests. Jan is free and open source under the AGPLv3 license.

recent_posts.summary: Insecure vibes are subconscious signals of anxiety, nervousness, or uncertainty that can negatively impact your interactions. By recognizing and addressing insecure vibes, you can improve your writing, meetings, presentations, negotiations, and pitches.

recent_posts.title: Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF: locally hosted web application that allows you to perform various operations on PDF files
recent_posts.summary: Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF is a locally hosted web application that allows users to perform various operations on PDF files, such as splitting, merging, converting, reorganizing, and compressing. It also supports features like dark mode, custom download options, and API integration. The application uses technologies like Spring Boot, Thymeleaf, PDFBox, LibreOffice, and Docker.

recent_posts.title: Using Metrics to Measure Individual Developer Performance — Laura Tacho
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the metrics that should be used to measure the individual performance of developers on teams. It emphasizes the importance of using appropriate metrics and highlights the drawbacks of using certain common metrics. The post also provides guidance on how to develop an evidence-based performance management system and stresses the need to focus on outcomes rather than output. Overall, it emphasizes the importance of thoughtful and fair evaluation of individual performance.

recent_posts.title: Four Responses to Feedback
recent_posts.summary: Feedback is data about our impact on individuals. It reflects the giver's perspective. When receiving feedback, express appreciation for the positive, consider easy changes, attempt hard changes, and evaluate changes that may be too difficult. Responding to feedback can be done one-on-one, in small groups, or in larger settings.

recent_posts.title: OpenInterpreter/open-interpreter: A natural language interface for computers
recent_posts.summary: Open Interpreter is a natural language interface that allows users to run code locally and perform various tasks with ChatGPT-like interface in their terminal. It overcomes the limitations of OpenAI's Code Interpreter by providing full internet access, no time or file size restrictions, and the ability to use any package or library. Users can control their computer's general-purpose capabilities, such as editing photos, videos, and PDFs, performing research with a Chrome browser, and analyzing large datasets.
